newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products tumble on China meal news, funds.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products tumble on China meal news, funds.

text.p: Reports that Chinese ports are clogged with up to one million tonnes of soymeal sent CBOT soy product futures tumbling on Wednesday amid heavy fund selling, traders said.
"That's what took us down from the highs. This isn't friendly," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and CO. "They (China) are loaded down."

Traders told Reuters in Shanghai that massive supplies had left a glut of soymeal in Chinese ports and pushed domestic prices lower. "The market has dropped and buyers are stuck with the meal," one source said.
Funds sold at least 1,700 lots of soyoil. Traders said Griffin Trading sold an estimated 2,000 lots of March soyoil.
But losses were limited by commercial buying interest. ADM reportedly bought 1,000 lots of March soyoil, traders said.

On the day, ADM reportedly sold 250 lots of March soymeal and Chicago Corp sold 150 March, traders said. Continental Grain reportedly bought 50 lots of March and Produce Grain bought 50 lots of July, traders said.
Soyoil closed 0.12 to 0.05 cent per lb lower with March off 0.09 at 24.00. Soymeal ended $5.20 to $0.80 per ton lower with March down $1.80 at $236.30.

Soymeal volume was estimated at 21,000 lots, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 18,732 lots, CBOT reported. Soyoil volume was estimated at 15,000 lots, against Tuesday's actual 12,566 lots, according to CBOT data.
